title: The Qur’an
author: —
description: The primary scripture of Islam, believed to be the verbatim word of Allah revealed to the Prophet Muhammad ︺ over 23 years — the foundation of every other Islamic discipline.

title: Tafsir Ibn Kathīr (Abridged)
author: Ibn Kathīr (abridged by Al-Mubārakpūrī)
description: One of the most widely-read classical commentaries on the Qur’an, drawing on hadith and the understanding of the Companions to explain each passage.

title: Al-Arba‘īn al-Nawawiyya (Forty Hadith)
author: Imām al-Nawawī
description: Forty-two carefully selected hadith covering the essentials of Islamic practice and character — the traditional first hadith text for beginners.

title: Riyāḍ al-Ṣāliḥīn (Gardens of the Righteous)
author: Imām al-Nawawī
description: A comprehensive anthology of hadith on every dimension of Muslim life — manners, worship, family, and ethics — arranged thematically for easy study.

title: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī
author: Imām al-Bukhārī
description: Considered the most rigorously authenticated collection of hadith in Sunni Islam, compiled after over a decade of critical evaluation of narrations.

title: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim
author: Imām Muslim
description: The second of the two most authentic hadith collections, praised by scholars for its precise organisation and the inclusion of complete chains of transmission.

title: Al-Muwaṭṭa’
author: Imām Mālik ibn Anas
description: One of the earliest systematic collections of hadith and the legal practice of Madinah, compiled by the founder of the Maliki school of jurisprudence.

title: Sunan Abī Dāwūd
author: Abū Dāwūd al-Sijistānī
description: A major hadith collection focusing especially on legal rulings and religious practice, containing around 5,300 selected narrations.

title: Jāmi‘ al-Tirmidhī
author: Imām al-Tirmidhī
description: A major hadith collection notable for including grading commentary on each narration and covering topics from acts of worship to etiquette.

title: Sunan Ibn Mājah
author: Ibn Mājah
description: The sixth of the six canonical hadith collections, covering legal, ethical, and eschatological topics with a distinctive focus on jurisprudence.

title: Al-Raḥīq al-Makhtūm (The Sealed Nectar)
author: Ṣafīur-Raḥmān al-Mubārakpūrī
description: A prize-winning modern biography of the Prophet Muhammad ︺, covering his life from birth through the establishment of the Islamic state in Madinah.

title: In the Footsteps of the Prophet
author: Tariq Ramadan
description: A spiritually reflective biography of the Prophet that explores the inner dimensions of his character, his relationships, and the relevance of his example today.

title: The Fundamentals of Tawhid
author: Bilal Philips
description: A clear, accessible introduction to the Islamic concept of God's oneness — its categories, its implications, and what constitutes its negation.

title: Uṣūl al-Thalātha (The Three Fundamental Principles)
author: Muḥammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhāb
description: A concise classical text explaining the three foundational questions every Muslim should know: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet?

title: Fiqh al-Sunna
author: Sayyid Sābiq
description: A comprehensive practical guide to Islamic law rooted in Qur’an and hadith, covering purification, prayer, fasting, zakat, and pilgrimage in accessible language.
